# Weekly Update Deck Skill

Produce a single-file horizontal-swipe HTML deck for a weekly team update.

## Workflow

1. Read DESIGN.md.
2. Identify squad name, week range, and audience (squad-internal vs cross-functional).
3. Slides:
   1. Cover (squad + week + author + date)
   2. Headline (one sentence + one number that matters this week)
   3. What shipped (3–5 items, link-style affordance)
   4. In flight (3–5 items, owner avatars)
   5. Blocked (1–3 items + clear ask)
   6. Metrics that matter (1–2 inline charts)
   7. Asks for next week (named owners)
   8. Closing + thanks
4. Arrow keys or click navigation. Each slide is 100vw wide.

## Output contract

```
<artifact identifier="weekly-update-w42" type="text/html" title="Weekly Update — Growth · W42">
<!doctype html>...</artifact>
```

Data, KPI & Finance · standup
Week of Jul 6 · Ops & Growth standup

One number, one decision.

Metrics standup · Open Design growth & activation Prepared for Ops & Growth · Jul 9, 2026
01 / 08
Headline answer
41%Signup → first-render conversion, −6pp WoW

The stars are up. The unit economics aren't.

GitHub stars grew 1.3% WoW to 68.4K, but signup-to-first-render conversion fell to 41% from 47% — the third straight week that step alone has dropped.

02 / 08
Metric proof

The proof, line by line.

01Weekly active builders — 14,220 sessions, +4% WoWCore · Activation
02Signup → first-render conversion — 41%, −6pp WoWFunnel · Down
03BYOK agent connections — 9,800 linked keys across 21 agents, +2%Agents · Flat
04Plugin installs — 214,000 cumulative, +11,400 this weekDistribution
03 / 08
Driver tree

Why conversion slipped.

01Default agent timeout raised p95 render latency 8.1s → 14.4s
OD
0261% of the drop concentrates in Safari desktop, React-based templates
MRSL
03New od-reframe flow added one extra confirm step before render
CA
04Everything else — agent choice, BYOK setup, plugin discovery — flat WoW

04 / 08
The anomaly

One thing broke the pattern.

Safari desktop first-render latency nearly doubled.

Every other channel held steady or improved this week. Safari desktop alone jumped from 8.1s to 14.4s p95, and it's driving almost two-thirds of the conversion drop. That forces a call: roll back the od-reframe confirm step, or ship a Safari-specific render path before Friday's release cut.

Decision needed: roll back or patch by Thu 18:00
05 / 08
Forecast

If we don't fix it by Friday.

First-render conversion · 4-week trailing

Higher is better
41%
▼ −6pp this week, tracking to 33% by month end if unresolved

p95 render latency · Safari desktop

Lower is better
14.4s
▲ +78% WoW, breaches the 12s render SLA
06 / 08
Recommended move

The one decision, and who owns it.

ENEngineering

Ship the Safari-specific fallback render path by Thursday EOD.

Bypasses the timeout path causing the 14.4s p95 without touching the other 39% of the drop.

PMProduct

Pull the extra confirm step from od-reframe pending re-test.

It was added for clarity, not speed — re-run the A/B once the Safari fix lands.

GRGrowth

Hold paid acquisition spend flat until conversion clears 45%.

No point buying more traffic into a funnel step that's currently losing 6pp of it.

DAData

Split Safari desktop out of the funnel dashboard going forward.

This anomaly stayed hidden inside a blended average for two weeks — that can't repeat.

07 / 08
Decision

Ship the fallback, not more spend.

The data says one thing: fix the render path before we spend another dollar acquiring users into a slower funnel. Engineering owns Thursday's patch, Growth holds spend flat until conversion recovers, and Data splits Safari out so this doesn't hide again.
